newsitem.title: USA: CME feeder cattle set new highs, live cattle firm.
newsitem.headline: CME feeder cattle set new highs, live cattle firm.

text.p: CME feeder cattle futures rallied from early profit-taking pressure to post new contract highs in all months and close at nearly three-year highs. Live cattle followed on technical demand, traders said.

Feeder cattle closed 0.800 to 1.175 cents per lb higher with August up 0.900 at 80.400 cents after setting a new high of 80.500 cents. Live cattle finished 0.650 to 0.375 higher with August up most at 64.450 cents.
Feeder cattle futures shruged off early profit-taking and rallied to new highs on demand prompted by rising cash feeder markets and declining feed costs, traders said.

Fund demand and buy stops added to the rally to set new contract highs in all months. Corn futures set new contract lows at their lowest levels in two years, while the CME feeder cattle index moved up to a 34-month high. With the addition of a technical breakout, feeders ran up to new highs, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.10 at $78.44 per cwt, a new high for the move and highest price level since August 18, 1994.
Cargill Investor Services and E.D.&F. Man bought early while Refco and Dean Witter sold. Buying was general on the rally, pit sources said.

Light carryover technical buying provided support in live cattle early and prices moved up further when feeder cattle ran up to new highs and pork pits advanced late ahead of the Hogs and Pigs report. Technicals offset early fundamental pressure brought on by expected lower packer bids for fed cattle next week and declining boxed beef values, they said.
Early chart resistance at 64.000 cents in August gave way to the mixed buying and spillover from the rally in feeders to lift that month up to a 1-1/2 week high, they added.
Prudential Securities bought August early while R.J. O'Brien sold, pit sources said.
